problems.problem_text: A coin is tossed twice. Draw a tree diagram and find the probability of getting two heads.
problems.solution: First toss: H(1/2) or T(1/2). Second toss: H(1/2) or T(1/2). P(HH) = 1/2 × 1/2 = 1/4.

problems.problem_text: A fair spinner numbered 1 to 4 is spun twice. Find the probability of getting a 3 on the first spin and a 1 on the second spin.
A bag contains 2 red and 3 blue marbles. A marble is taken, replaced, then another is taken. Find the probability of picking two red marbles.
A fair spinner with colours red (R), blue (B), green (G) is spun twice. Find the probability of getting the same colour both times.
The probability that it rains on any given day is 0.4. Using a tree diagram, find the probability that it rains on exactly one of the next two days.
A bag contains 3 red and 2 blue sweets. Two sweets are taken without replacement. Draw a tree diagram and find the probability that both sweets are red.
problems.solution: P(first red) = 3/5. After removing 1 red: 2 red, 2 blue remain. P(second red | first red) = 2/4 = 1/2. P(both red) = 3/5 × 1/2 = 3/10.

problems.problem_text: A bag contains 3 red and 2 blue sweets. Two sweets are taken without replacement. Find the probability that they are different colours.
The probability that a seed germinates is 0.8. Three seeds are planted. Find the probability that all three germinate.
In a game, the probability of winning a prize is 0.3. A player plays the game twice. Find the probability that the player wins exactly one prize.
A box contains 4 red pens and 6 blue pens. Two pens are taken without replacement. Find the probability that both pens are the same colour.
A bag contains 5 red, 3 green and 2 yellow marbles. Two marbles are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that both marbles are green.
problems.solution: Total = 10. P(first green) = 3/10. After removing 1 green: 2 green left. P(second green | first green) = 2/9. P(both green) = 3/10 × 2/9 = 6/90 = 1/15.

problems.problem_text: A bag contains 5 red, 3 green and 2 yellow marbles. Two marbles are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that the two marbles are of different colours.
A bag contains 4 white and 6 black balls. Three balls are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that at least one ball is white.
A bag contains 3 red and 7 blue marbles. Two marbles are drawn. Find the probability that the second marble is blue, given that the first marble drawn was red and not replaced.
problems.solution: After removing 1 red: 2 red, 7 blue remain. P(second blue | first red) = 7/9.

problems.problem_text: A box contains 2 red, 3 white and 5 green balls. Three balls are drawn without replacement. Find the probability that the three balls are all different colours.
problems.solution: Total = 10. Each ordering of R,W,G: P = 2/10 × 3/9 × 5/8 = 30/720 = 1/24. Number of orderings = 3! = 6. Total = 6 × 1/24 = 6/24 = 1/4.

problems.problem_text: In a school, the probability that a student studies Mathematics is 0.6, Physics is 0.5, and Chemistry is 0.4. The choices are independent. Find the probability that a student studies exactly two of these three subjects.
